list.item: Participants compete by proposing solutions that address the Saudi market.
Participants choose one of the pre-selected domains.
Each team supplies its own problem statement and solution within its chosen domain.
Problem context: Satellites may be endangered by fluctuating space weather.
Required approach: Provide an analytical solution using AI and Machine Learning.
Required focus: Study a specific effect on the satellite.
Required output/use: Give ground control insight about possible effects to support decision-making.

section.title: 2. Non-Terrestrial Connection in Rural Working Areas

list.item: Problem context: Many work sites in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) lack ground infrastructure for seamless connectivity.
Required approach: Propose a solution for specific areas.
Required outcome: Ensure seamless connectivity while protecting the working company's data.
Definition: Gathering, processing, and analyzing data about the planet's physical, chemical, and biological systems using satellites and sensors positioned in space.
Examples of data/content: Imagery of natural terrain, pollution, and weather patterns.
Example application areas: Urban planning, natural disaster monitoring and warning, and weather-pattern monitoring. These are examples, not an exhaustive list.
Required approach: Provide an analytical solution using AI or Machine Learning for a given context.
Required use: Help decision-making.
Data types named in the source: Hyperspectral, SAR/InSar, thermal, and optical data.

section.title: 4. Application of Space Technologies in Other Sectors

list.item: Use any space technology to address an issue in another sector of the Saudi market.
The technology does not need to be present in the Saudi space sector.
The problem it solves must occur in another sector within the Saudi market.
Students complete the participation form.
In the form, they briefly describe their problem and proposed solution.
Based on submitted ideas, 12 teams qualify for Day 1.
At the end of Day 1, AI agents judge submissions against a published rubric.
Six teams qualify for Day 2.
On Day 2, teams present their solutions to human judges.
Human judges choose the top three teams.

section.title: Prizes
section.paragraph: The invitation also states that winning solutions might eventually be commercialized and used in the space industry. Winners will be connected to experts in the sector.

section.title: Judging criteria named in the invitation

list.item: Specificity of the problem
Effectiveness and novelty of the solution
Relevance of the solution to the Saudi market

section.paragraph: The separate rubric defines the complete weighted criteria and scoring details.

SSA Annual Report
